dedupe_keys.name: aerial imagery object identification dataset for building and road detection and building height estimation 9 u s cities

description: This collection is a training and test set for detecting buildings and roads in aerial imagery and estimating building heights, covering 25 locations in nine U.S. cities: Arlington (Massachusetts), Atlanta, Austin, Washington DC, New Haven, New York City, Norfolk, San Francisco and Seekonk. It was assembled in 2016 by Kyle Bradbury and colleagues at Duke University's Energy Initiative and published on figshare, with one dataset per city. It combines high-resolution aerial imagery from the United States Geological Survey, over 40,000 building footprints and road polylines from OpenStreetMap as annotations, and LiDAR height data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Access: open download from figshare, with a metadata document that describes the data in full. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution for the collection, while the OpenStreetMap shapefiles remain under the Open Database License; free. Caveats: annotations are OpenStreetMap outlines that may be misaligned or incomplete, and imagery dates from around 2016. Simulation uses are training building-extraction and height models that feed exposure inventories and 3D city models. Related records: the IEEE GRSS DFC23 roof-type benchmark and GlobalBuildingAtlas.
